WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT CLAIM.
1. No centimetre figures. The illustration carries no printed dimension callout, so no real-world size is recoverable. Everything above is a ratio against waistband depth.
2. I nearly made the "measured the wrong feature" mistake. The red marker's raw bounding box is 75 x 486px and its PCA minor-axis extent is 45px — but the red is a THICK annotation stroke (13-18px each side) around a ~10px white interior. Using 45px as "welt width" would have made the render look 47% too narrow. The correct comparable is the stroke centreline-to-centreline distance, 26.0px horizontal / 25.9px perpendicular, which matches the render within 8%. The 45px number is the annotation, not the garment.
3. I could NOT reliably compare HORIZONTAL proportions, and no single scale factor reconciles them: render/drawing ratio is 0.92 for welt strip width, 0.68 for welt-right-edge-to-crease distance, and 1.60 for belt-loop width. Foreshortening in a strongly oblique photograph would push all three the same direction; these go opposite ways, which means the freehand sketch is not internally consistent at better than about +/-30% on horizontal secondary features. I therefore raised no finding on horizontal spacing and treat only the vertical-axis measurements (length, top/bottom gap), which share an axis with the waistband-depth landmark, as trustworthy.
4. Saturation was checked. The render welt (411px) was measured inside a 500px-tall trace window and the illustration's black hip welt was re-measured after an initial crop clipped its bounding box at the crop edge (ymin=280 = crop boundary) and a belt-loop stroke inflated its apparent depth to 90px; edge-tracing the two long lines separately gives the true 34.3px. The first number would have been 2.6x wrong.
5. Line C in the render (x=397 at y=440) was verified to be the trouser CREASE, not part of the pocket: its darkness persists at full strength through y=200-700 while lines A and B fade out at y=243 and y=650.
6. Belt-loop COUNT is reported as a match (3 loops + 1 descending seam line in both) with low confidence — the drawing's leftmost loop shares a stroke with the leg silhouette and cannot be separated cleanly.
